title: Where Commands Start
objective: Understand how gsd-tools.cjs receives commands and begins processing them

content.value:
Every GSD command enters through a single file: get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs. This is the entry point. When a workflow or agent needs to interact with GSD, it runs:

  node gsd-tools.cjs <command> [args] [--raw]

The entry point does three things:
1. Requires all the library modules (state, phase, roadmap, config, etc.)
2. Determines the current working directory (cwd)
3. Reads the command from process.argv and dispatches it

Notice how each require() loads a specific domain module. This is GSD's module boundary pattern: each .cjs file owns one area of functionality. There are no barrel files or index.cjs re-exports — each module explicitly requires what it needs.

The --raw flag controls output format: without it, GSD outputs JSON; with it, GSD outputs plain text. This dual-mode output lets both machines (JSON parsing) and humans (readable text) use the same commands.

successCriteria: You can identify gsd-tools.cjs as the single entry point and explain the role of cwd, args, and the --raw flag
